cli.doctor.fix.explain:
For mKey to see key presses and press keys for you, the system needs one permission. mKey will install input device access rules (method: {method}) and enable the uinput virtual input kernel module. This requires administrator rights.

Note: after that, programs running as your user will be able to read key presses. All programs of this kind work this way.

cli.root.long:
mKey records and replays keyboard, mouse and touch actions, reacts to hotkeys, windows and pixel colors, and creates virtual input devices.

Run "mkey gui" to open the web interface, or "mkey help <command>" for help on a command.
cli.root.short: Input macro tool for Linux (X11 and Wayland)

cli.send.long:
Run a macro written in the mKey language.

Examples:
  mkey send '{Enter}'                          press Enter
  mkey send '^{Ctrl}{C}~{Ctrl}'                copy (Ctrl+C)
  mkey send '{"Hello!"}'                       type text
  mkey send '^{Shift}{"Hello, Vera!"}~{Shift}'  type in capitals
  mkey send --delay 3s '{"Hello"}'             wait 3 seconds, then type

The macro runs in the currently active window. Syntax: docs/dsl.md.

Done! mKey is installed.

What next:
  • The "mKey" icon is in the application menu.
  • Example with an autoclicker and hotkeys: mkey project enable example
  • Emergency stop of everything: Esc + Backspace + Enter together.
  • System check: mkey doctor
  • Uninstall: mkey uninstall

The wizard will install the program in a few steps. Before each change it explains what will happen and asks for your consent.
